title: reserved-pool-proactive-triage-and-patch-for-burst-failure-mode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Two enterprise customers reported intermittent 429s and queued requests during bursts over the weekend despite reserved pools reporting available headroom. Initial investigation showed autoscaler accepted burst requests but later reclaimed slots, causing silent capacity shortfalls. This ticket documents a proactive full-triage, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and the patch rollout plan to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-07 21:40 UTC: Customer A (FinRegCorp) page — high 429 rate on dedicated region eu-west-1 during scheduled batch jobs.
2026-03-07 22:05 UTC: Oncall routed to dedicated-autoscaler team. Initial mitigation: increased temporary burst limit for FinRegCorp via admin override.
2026-03-08 03:12 UTC: Customer B (HealthML Inc) reported similar symptoms in us-east-1 during overnight retraining window.
2026-03-08 04:00 UTC: PagerDuty escalation to SRE and Serving Runtime. Hotfix plan drafted to add conservative min_headroom and extend grace-window for burst credit accounting.
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: Repro harness created and noisy metrics captured against staging reserved pools. Reproduction consistent with production under synthetic burst pattern.
2026-03-12 14:30 UTC: Root cause hypothesis validated in staging. Patch implemented and code review started (PR linked).
2026-03-14 10:00 UTC: Canary rollout scheduled for dedicated-2026.03.2 to two small reserved pools; monitoring checks added.
reproduction_steps: 1) Provision a reserved pool with headroom target = 20 slots and burst_limit = 50 tokens/sec.
2) Start steady baseline traffic consuming 70% of committed slots.
3) Inject burst traffic with a short high-rate spike that does many small allocations across tenants to force the burst accounting path.
4) Simulate a 6-12s metric ingestion delay by delaying the autoscaler metrics consumer to replicate telemetry lag.

5) Observe: autoscaler transiently accepts allocations then reclaims slots when the delayed burst-credit reconciliation runs, leading to in-flight allocations being dropped or preempted and 429s at the API layer.
root_cause_summary: A multi-factor failure: (A) burst-credit ledger math used integer truncation when aggregating per-tenant micro-allocations which led to cumulative undercounting of available burst credits; (B) the autoscaler relies on a metrics ingestion window with optimistic assumptions (5s) — when ingestion had 6-12s lag under noisy telemetry the reconciler mis-estimated live headroom; (C) a race between the allocation path and the late reconciler allowed allocations to be accepted but later revoked by reclamation logic that assumed stale metrics. Together these caused silent shortfalls despite dashboards showing nominal pool headroom.
impact_analysis: Affected 2 enterprise customers during low-traffic hours; approximately 3-7% of requests for their reserved tenancy returned 429/TEMP_UNAVAILABLE during bursts. Economic impact: increased latency for critical jobs, customer SLAs at risk. Root cause not a hardware shortage but software accounting + telemetry race causing spurious reclamation.
mitigation_plan: Short-term: deploy admin overrides to increase burst_limit for impacted tenants and enable conservative min_headroom (default +3 slots) for all dedicated pools. Mid-term patch: fix rounding bug in ledger aggregator, extend reconciliation window boundary checks, and add 'allocation-confirmation' handshake to avoid immediate reclamation of just-allocated slots. Long-term: add stronger invariants and alerts when reclamation rescinds >1% of recent allocations in a 1m window.

https://github.com/redwood-inference/pool-autoscaler/pull/12346 - feat: allocation-confirmation handshake and safety guard for reclamation
https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-consumer/pull/987 - fix: graceful backoff on metrics lag to avoid stale reconciliations
testing_and_rollout: Unit + property tests added for ledger aggregation covering thousands of micro-allocations.
Staging: 72h soak with synthetic burst patterns and simulated metric delays; validation of no reclamation spikes.
Canary: deploy dedicated-2026.03.2 to 2 small reserved pools on us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for 12 hours; automated checks: reclaimed_allocations_rate < 0.1%, burst_success_rate >= 99.9%.
Full rollout plan: 25% pools -> 50% -> 100% over 6 hours with rollback gates if reclaimed_allocations_rate > 0.5% or customer error rate increases.
Rollback: revert to dedicated-2026.03.1 and re-enable admin override while the team investigates failures.
post_deploy_checks: Alert: ReclamationBurstAlert fires if reclaimed_allocations_count > 10 in 5m for a single pool.
Dashboard: dedicated/pools/headroom-adjusted and dedicated/pools/reclaimed_allocations_rate updated to show pre/post patch comparisons.
SLO check: monitor per-tenant 429 rate and tail latency for 48h post-rollout.
customer_communications: 2026-03-08: Initial acknowledgement sent to FinRegCorp and HealthML Inc with 'we are investigating' and admin override applied; ticket links included.
2026-03-12: Customer update: identified accounting mismatch and plan to deploy patch; ETA 2026-03-14.
2026-03-14: Post-deploy note: canary shows improvement; propose coordinated validation window with each customer to confirm end-to-end behavior and to close incidents.
runbook_updates: Added 'Burst reconciliation lag' section to dedicated-autoscaler-runbook with steps to apply admin override, how to safely increase min_headroom, and how to perform fast rollback.
monitoring_notes: Primary telemetry gaps discovered in metrics_consumer lag and aggregation rounding. Added synthetic check that injects controlled micro-allocations every 5m and verifies ledger consistency. New monitor 'ledger-consistency-check' alerts on any discrepancy > 0.5%.

notes: This incident differs from recent autoscaler issues: it's not pure load forecasting or preemption policy bugs but an intersection of ledger arithmetic, telemetry lag, and reclamation race. The fix is intentionally conservative to avoid oscillation. Keep customers informed and offer credits if SLA thresholds were missed after verification.
